Hi Soojin,

We just signed up for a trial via your self-serve flow (company: Orchard Analytics). I'm Alex, Head of Platform at Orchard — we ingest lots of user queries and are evaluating hosted inference providers to replace our current on-prem setup.

High level:
- Use case: multi-tenant real-time ranking + semantic search for customer support (mix of short chat replies and longer context-aware summaries)
- Daily traffic: ~1.2M requests/day (currently 4–6M tokens/day)
- Peak concurrency: ~120 concurrent requests during business hours
- Timeline: pilot in Jan, production by end of Q2 2027

Would love a short demo of the hosted API and any docs on throughput/cost tradeoffs. Prefer PST mornings for scheduling.

Thanks,
Alex

alex@orchard.ai

Hi Alex — thanks for signing up and for the helpful context. I'm Soojin on the Solutions Development team at Redwood — I'll run the quick qualification and get a demo on the calendar with one of our AEs. A couple quick questions so we tailor the walkthrough: 

1) Traffic profile: is the 1.2M requests/day spread fairly evenly or is it bursty (spikes during support hours)? any % of requests that are >1k tokens?
2) Latency SLOs: are you aiming for p95 <200ms tail, or is higher latency acceptable if cost is lower?
3) Data sensitivity: will user PII or regulated data be sent? (this affects Private/Dedicated recommendations)
4) Auth/SSO: do you need SSO/SAML for the Redwood Console?
5) Pilot scope: for Jan pilot — is it limited to a single team or a cross-product bet?

If you can reply with short answers, I'll propose three PST morning slots. I've attached a short demo agenda so you know what we'll cover.

Best,
Soojin Lee
SDR, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

--

From: Alex Rivera <alex@orchard.ai>

Date: 2026-11-12T12:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Looking to schedule a quick demo — started self-serve signup

Hi Soojin — quick answers below: 
1) Burstiness: fairly bursty — median traffic is steady but we get spikes ~2–3x during product launches; about 5% of requests are long (1k+ tokens) mainly for summary generation.
2) Latency SLO: target p95 ~250ms, p99 can be higher; we prefer predictable cost over ultra-low tail latency.
3) Data sensitivity: some PII (emails, ticket text); SOC2 + encryption-at-rest important.
4) Auth/SSO: yes, need SSO for team access to the Console but not required for API keys during pilot.
5) Pilot: starting with Customer Support team (single team) and expanding if results are positive.

Time preference: PST mornings work; next week Tue/Wed/Thu mornings generally open.

Thanks,
Alex
